title: What the Reopening of Nathu La Means for China-India Relations
author: Siddharth Singh
text:
The China-India border post at the Nathu La pass as viewed in 2011.
Credit: Wikimedia Commons/Indrajit Das
The last six years have been a testing time for China-India relations. The boundary crisis in Eastern Ladakh in 2020, along with the loss of lives in the Galwan Valley in June 2020, brought the bilateral relationship to its lowest levels in decades. Trade through Nathu La, a mountain pass through the Himalayas linking India’s Sikkim state with Tibet, also stopped in 2020. The meeting between Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar with China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Manila on July 22 focused on peace on the border and practical trade cooperation. A few days later, it was announced that the Nathu La pass would be reopened from August 1. This sequence of events is part of the cautious diplomacy that is now taking shape where serious differences will remain but some practical cooperation is slowly being restored.[...]
